questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to try and live in Berlin as I have been there some times before and really liked the city, so an exchange semester in Berlin seemed like the perfect opportunity to do that

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy to find the information you needed, I wasn't really in doubt about anything

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: E-mails containing information and orientation days at the university. I also had the impression that the incoming office at FU was ready to help and answer questions if you needed anything

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in a dormitory connected to the Danish Church in Berlin - it was quite easy for me to get a room there, but there is only 4 rooms so it is not a big dorm. I just found their website and wrote them an e-mail.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They have the same problems with housing in Berlin as in Copenhagen, so my impression was that it can be difficult to find affordable housing. But everyone I knew managed to find something so it is not like it is impossible

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for the courses you want to sign up for through a platform called Campus Management and then you get assigned to the courses after the deadline. However, it wasn't possible for me to register for all the courses I wanted and needed through Campus Management, and in this case you have to write the lecturer of the course. It is also possible to reregister for courses during the first two weeks of the semester if you change your mind about which courses you want, as long as there are available spots in the course

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mails from the university with information and the orientation days, where the registration process was demonstrated and you could ask questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There were two courses I wanted that was filled up when I wrote the lecturer of the courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I thought it was a little hard to make your schedule yourself and choose between the courses but everything worked out in the end, so my advice would be to not stress so much about it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think it was fine

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of the sociology courses at FU are seminars with a maximum of 18 students and these are more dicussion-based

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Globalization of Science - A Gender Perspective, Religiosity of European Societies, Islamist Extremism and Radicalization, Introduction to Social and Religious Movements, Throwback: Cultural Shifts towards Regression, Nostalgia and Deceleration and Measuring Social Constructs

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found all the courses interesting but I would recommend the course called "Throwback: Cultural Shifts towards Regression, Nostalgia and Deceleration" in particular

questions.answer: I didn't attend the sports activities

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city and everything it has to offer

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to adjust

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find the cultural differences challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Attend the German Vorkurs offered by FU before the semester starts - this is where I met most of the people I hung out with during my exchange. 2) Try and make a schedule where you don't go to the university every day so you also have some days "off" to enjoy and explore the city. 3) Take advantage of the opportunity to choose some courses on subjects that you wouldn't normally be introduced to

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To try and live in another country and to study at another university

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't really find anything in particular challenging, other that being away from family and friends and being "out of your comfortzone" but that is a part of being on exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
